test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A ray of light passing or appear to pass through the principal focus of a concave/convex mirror after reflection ______

options.text: will emerge perpendicular to the principal axis
will emerge perpendicular to the principal axis, only in the case of concave mirror
will emerge perpendicular to the principal axis, only in the case of convex mirror
will emerge parallel to the principal axis

solution:
The correct answer is __**will emerge parallel to the principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A ray of light that passes through or appears to pass through the principal focus of a concave or convex mirror will reflect and become parallel to the principal axis.
 
• This behavior is a result of the laws of reflection where the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
 
• In concave mirrors, the principal focus is a real point where parallel rays converge after reflection.
 
• In convex mirrors, the principal focus is a virtual point from which parallel rays appear to diverge after reflection.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Principal Axis**: It is the line passing through the center of curvature and the pole of the mirror.
 
• **Principal Focus**: The point where rays parallel to the principal axis converge (concave) or appear to diverge from (convex) after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• **Focal Length**: The distance between the principal focus and the pole of the mirror. It is half the radius of curvature.
 
• **Concave Mirror**: A spherical mirror that curves inward, reflecting light inward to one focal point.
 
• **Convex Mirror**: A spherical mirror that curves outward, causing reflected light to diverge, making the focus appear behind the mirror.
